players.product: AI cluster design/integration & managed services (plus Smart Modular memory)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Mark Adams and CFO Nate Olmstead: Q1 FY2026 net sales were $343 million, up 2% sequentially and 1% year-over-year, even though Penguin recognized no hyperscale hardware revenue in the quarter (a meaningful contributor a year earlier). Non-GAAP gross margin was 30% (down 0.8 percentage points YoY, mainly from the wind-down of the high-margin Penguin Edge business); non-GAAP operating income was $42 million (up 1% YoY), the sixth straight quarter of YoY non-GAAP operating margin expansion; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.49, flat YoY. Segment mix: Advanced Computing 44%, Integrated Memory 40%, Optimized LED (Cree LED brand) $55 million (16%), described as down 18% (sequentially by the CEO, year-over-year by the CFO) on weak China demand and softness at certain large U.S. OEM customers. Services net sales were $65 million (down 9%) and product net sales $279 million (up 3%). In late December Penguin agreed to sell its remaining 19% stake in Zilia Technologies (formerly SMART Modular do Brazil) for $46 million, expected to close in fiscal Q3 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $343 million, up 1% year-over-year; non-GAAP gross margin 30%; non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.49

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced Computing Q1 net sales were $151 million (44% of company), up 9% sequentially but down 15% year-over-year, reflecting the Penguin Edge wind-down and hyperscale hardware sales in Q1 last year that did not recur; excluding Penguin Edge and hyperscale hardware, segment net sales grew 52% year-over-year. Q1 bookings included two new Penguin customers, one in the defense sector and one in education and research, and the pipeline is expanding into financial services, oil and gas, telecommunications, manufacturing and education. Penguin launched a rapid development workshop program to help prospects plan AI at scale, and is building a Penguin software stack that combines its ICE ClusterWare platform with best-of-breed open and third-party software components (including software from companies like NVIDIA) covering cluster management, security and orchestration.
quarterly_data.figure: Advanced Computing $151 million, down 15% year-over-year; excluding Penguin Edge and hyperscale hardware grew 52% year-over-year

quarterly_data.signal: Integrated Memory Q1 net sales were $137 million (40% of company), up 3% sequentially and 41% year-over-year; heading into Q2, demand signals are strong across networking, telecommunications and computing customers. Beyond the core customer migration to DDR5, customers are evaluating how best to use memory to optimize AI compute performance, and besides legacy OEM customers Penguin is seeing sales growth in direct-to-enterprise engagements and in large hyperscale customers. The CFO said the raised full-year memory outlook is 'due to some benefits from pricing primarily', with overall demand 'very strong and healthy'; memory sales carry a lower gross margin than the company average.

CXL and optical memory: Penguin, an early developer of Compute Express Link (CXL) solutions for high-speed GPU/CPU-to-device and GPU/CPU-to-memory connections, is 'currently shipping early production units through our OEM partners while continuing to expand end-user qualification efforts'; future CXL versions are expected to emphasize memory pooling. In parallel it continues to invest in the design of its optical memory appliance (OMA) in collaboration with key technology partners, using a photonic transport layer to raise GPU, CPU and memory interconnect performance. Asked about Marvell's acquisition of Celestial AI and the shift toward optical fabrics, the CEO said Penguin is not seeing any changes but called the deal 'a strong validation of the market opportunity' that supports its strategy of developing that type of system-level memory product.

FY2026 outlook confirmed at the midpoint: 6% net sales growth and $2 of non-GAAP diluted EPS (plus or minus $0.25), still assuming no Advanced Computing hardware sales to hyperscale customers and Penguin Edge sales essentially ceasing by the end of fiscal 2026 (together approximately a 14 percentage point unfavorable impact on total net sales growth and approximately 30 points on Advanced Computing). Approximately 53% to 54% of net sales are expected in the second half as pipeline AI opportunities are assumed to book and ship then; Advanced Computing and LED are expected to be down sequentially from Q1 to Q2. By segment: Advanced Computing between minus 15% and plus 15%; Memory raised to grow between 20% and 35%; LED lowered to decline between minus 15% and minus 5%. The non-GAAP gross margin outlook was cut by 50 basis points to 29%, plus or minus 1 percentage point, on a higher mix of lower-margin memory sales; non-GAAP operating expenses are expected at $250 million, plus or minus $10 million.
quarterly_data.figure: 6% net sales growth and $2 of non-GAAP diluted EPS (midpoint); Memory between 20% and 35%; Advanced Computing between minus 15% and plus 15%; non-GAAP gross margin 29%

quarterly_data.signal: Supply constraints: the FY2026 outlook contemplates 'ongoing supply chain constraints, especially as they relate to our Advanced Computing and Integrated Memory businesses', including extended lead times for certain components that affect how quickly existing and new customer projects ramp. The CEO said Penguin continues 'to do a fairly good job navigating the supply constraints' in memory and has not seen anything material impacting that business; the CFO said 'our ability to procure supply is going to be one of the key variables' for the full-year memory outlook, that second-half memory strength is contingent on securing supply, and that in 'today's constrained memory environment' Penguin will look for opportunities to secure some supply to take risk off the table, backed by its balance sheet. Inventory fell to $213 million from $247 million a year ago on order and shipment linearity (days of inventory 38 days), although rising memory prices lift inventory cost; Penguin generally buys to orders rather than to forecast.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory $213 million; days of inventory 38 days

quarterly_data.signal: New-customer conversions and pipeline: the award from a major financial institution announced last quarter is now a signed agreement, with the PO expected 'shortly this week or worst case next', and Penguin has signed a master agreement with 'a major new oil and gas customer', with a PO expected in the next week or so. For first-time customers the award, master agreement, PO, component sourcing and staging sequence makes quarterly timing harder to predict, which is why Q2 and second-half guidance is cautious. Penguin is in discussions with sovereign cloud customers outside the U.S. about potential large-scale AI deployments ('a few new sovereign cloud opportunities of large scale' are in the pipeline), and the CEO said enterprise AI opportunities have been accelerating over the last 6 to 12 months as spending shifts from hyperscaler large language model training toward enterprise production rollouts, with early signs of workloads moving toward inference.

Channel and ecosystem: management said it remains focused on strengthening its partnerships with 'ecosystem partners such as NVIDIA, AMD and CDW'. On CDW, the CEO said Penguin's AI factory and large-scale deployment capabilities are 'a great addition to CDW's capabilities and competencies', and customer opportunities for Penguin's managed services and software at large-scale customers are represented in the pipeline.

connects_to.relationship: Penguin designs, builds, deploys and manages full-stack NVIDIA-based AI factory infrastructure (NVIDIA AI Factory Specialized Partner)

contracts.signal: CEO Mark Adams: the NVIDIA relationship 'continues to get stronger and stronger as the enterprise deployments scale and grow in number'; as a services solutions provider for NVIDIA-based AI factories Penguin is well positioned and is evaluating how to bring the best of what it does with NVIDIA into a long-term strategic solution offering. Penguin is also working with companies like NVIDIA to include their software in its customized ICE ClusterWare-based software platform.
